challenge.title: Reforms and Ideas Evidence Challenge
challenge.description: Complete 10 activities: six clue-and-conclusion decisions and four matching tasks. Choose a supporting clue and its conclusion for each evidence decision; both parts count together as one activity. Get at least 7 activities correct. All supplied lesson clues are available without saving them in your journal.

badge.name: Reforms and Ideas Investigator
badge.description: Earned by completing all four Chapter 13 missions and passing the evidence challenge. Recognizes careful connections between changes, reforms, ideas and local concerns.

evidence.question: A timeline labels 1801 as part of the 18th century. Which clue directly checks the boundary?
choices: 1801 begins the 19th century
1801 ends the 18th century
All years beginning with 18 are in the 18th century
A century has no boundary
evidence.explanation: The 18th century is 1701-1800. The year 1801 begins the next century.

evidence.question: Which clue tells you when the monopoly was formally put into operation, rather than when its decree was issued?
choices: Formal establishment followed in March 1782
The royal decree and operation always began together
Every local effect happened in 1780
The founding of an unrelated society dates its operation
evidence.explanation: Decision and implementation are different stages: the decree was dated 1780 and formal establishment followed in March 1782.

evidence.question: A report treats rising government income as proof that every household was better off. Which clue directly checks this?
choices: Government income alone does not measure household wellbeing
Income proves every household had equal benefits
All producers had the same experience
A government goal removes every burden
evidence.explanation: Income and household experience answer different questions. Investigate requirements and effects on people as well as revenue.

evidence.question: You need the date on the royal company charter. Which clue directly supplies it?
choices: The charter is dated 10 March 1785
Every economic institution began in 1781
The charter was issued in 1812
The date of a different policy gives its date
evidence.explanation: Keep each document attached to its own date. The company charter is dated 10 March 1785.

evidence.question: A newspaper founding date is used to claim one issue printed a particular rights text. Which clue directly checks that claim?
choices: A publication date does not prove a particular issues contents
Every newspaper printed every declaration
The founding date proves what every reader believed
An outlet date proves universal agreement
evidence.explanation: Check the issue itself before claiming what it contained. Publication, receipt and response are separate questions.

evidence.question: Two records contain similar complaints. Which clue directly checks whether they prove one national plan?
choices: A shared grievance does not automatically establish one national plan
All similar complaints prove coordination
Every request demanded independence
All residents held identical beliefs
evidence.explanation: A shared concern supports comparison. Coordination or a common national program requires additional evidence.

matching.question: Match each investigation word with its meaning.
pairs: Who governs or controls a place
matching.explanation: Trade, authority and implementation describe different parts of economic and political change.

matching.question: Match each example with the kind of evidence it provides.
pairs: An institution linked with economic knowledge
An official document establishing an organization
matching.explanation: These examples show different methods and institutions; their existence alone does not establish equal benefits.

matching.question: Match the dated examples with the right description.
matching.explanation: Keep a declaration, a newspaper outlet and a constitution separate. Their dates do not reveal every readers response.

matching.question: Match each case or question with the recorded action or evidence it needs.
pairs: Petition for relief from tribute-collection duties
Uprising linked with government control of a local product
Comparison across dated records of concerns and actions
matching.explanation: A petition and an uprising are different responses. Broader claims about change over time need dated comparisons.
